main_body: A small brown gnarled tree-stump / root cluster with a few green moss patches, drawn on a stone-tile background, about 16x15 px
top_band: none - no distinct horizontal top surface; a brown mass of trunk and branches with dark outlines and small green moss patches
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: dark brown outline, then mid-brown trunk and branch forms with darker brown shadows down to the base. There is no lighter horizontal band, no front-edge line and no eave shadow. The object is an organic silhouette seen face-on with no distinct top surface, so it does not show the top-plus-front structure of the 3/4 contract. It is also a gnarled stump rather than a canopy tree, and the gray stone cells around it make the shape hard to read.

style.evidence: The reference trees have a rich canopy with 5-6 greens, per-clump highlights and a detailed root flare. The candidate is a small, tangled brown shape with about 3 brown steps and a few green moss dabs. Its outline is dark brown and fairly tinted, which is good, but the body is mostly flat brown with little grain, and it has no canopy. Its tiles carry only a few colours each, far below the reference density, so it reads as much thinner than the reference.
